title: smithable.yml
description: Describes what a Smithable application does. See docs/spec.

smithable.title: Spec format version
smithable.description: The spec format version this file is written in.

app.title: The app
app.description: The app's name, what it is for, its currency and its time zone.

name.title: Name
name.description: The app's name, shown in its header, its tab and its mails.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: The currency of the app's amounts, as its ISO 4217 code, e.g. EUR.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.description: The time zone dates and times are shown in, as its IANA name, e.g. Europe/Mariehamn.

description.title: What it is for
description.description: What this is, in a sentence. Read by the models that draft and change the app and by its assistants, and the app's own description is the landing page's and the API's; not shown to visitors otherwise.

intent.title: What it should achieve
intent.description: The outcome or experience this should achieve, in a sentence: it guides the models that change the app, and it is the summary's sentence for this part.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Domain rules in plain language. A rule does nothing by itself until something implements it: the models read them when drafting and changing the app, and the advice notes point at them.
examples: An order over 1000 needs a manager's approval before it ships.

id.description: A short name to refer to the rule by.

models.description: The data the application stores. Model names are PascalCase.

fields.description: What a record holds: each field's name and its type.

oneOf.description: A type with optional "!" (required), "unique" and "= default", e.g. "string!" or "int! = 60". Or choices: "draft | sent | paid" (the first is the default).

type.description: What the field holds: a type (string, money, date, …), another model (Customer, or Order[] for all that refer here), or choices ("draft | sent | paid").

required.description: A record cannot be saved without it; or a condition, e.g. { status: [inProgress, closed] }: required while the record fits it.

by.description: app: the form never shows it; its default (a value, or ME()), an action, an incoming entry or code fills it.

sequence.description: On an int!: the app gives each new record the next number after the highest (an order or invoice number); the form never shows it.

locked.description: true: set when the record is made, never changed after; or a condition, e.g. { status: closed }: read-only while the record fits it. An action's set may still change it.

unique.description: No two records may hold the same value: true (among one owner's records when records are read by their owners only, else in the whole app), owner or app to say which outright.

default.description: For choices, "none" means no default. ME() on a field that refers to User: who makes the record.

min.description: The smallest number allowed; for a text, its shortest length.

max.description: The largest number allowed; for a text, its longest length.

formula.description: Computes the value, spreadsheet-style, e.g. "quantity * unitPrice" or "SUM(lines.amount)".

examples.description: Inputs and the expected result of the formula; each becomes a test.

input.description: The values of the fields the formula reads.

expected.description: What the formula must give for them.

description.title: What it is for
description.description: What this is, in a sentence. Read by the models that draft and change the app and by its assistants, and the app's own description is the landing page's and the API's; not shown to visitors otherwise.

intent.title: What it should achieve
intent.description: The outcome or experience this should achieve, in a sentence: it guides the models that change the app, and it is the summary's sentence for this part.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Domain rules in plain language. A rule does nothing by itself until something implements it: the models read them when drafting and changing the app, and the advice notes point at them.
examples: An order over 1000 needs a manager's approval before it ships.

id.description: A short name to refer to the rule by.

ownedBy.description: A User field whose user owns the record, instead of its creator.

review.description: Pictures and files that wait for a reviewer before others see them: all (every picture and file field) or a list of them. A required one holds the whole record until it is approved; an optional one only the file.

trash.description: Deleted records stay in a trash for thirty days, where whoever may delete them can restore them; then they are removed for good.

namedBy.description: What names a record, its title wherever one record is shown or referred to: a field (a text, a choice, a date, a number, an amount), a reference (that record's own name) or a field one reference away (classType.name), or a list of such parts joined with " · " ([classType, startsAt]). Left out, the first short text field is the title, else the first long text, else the record's number.

thread.description: The records as messages of a conversation (a page shows a list of them as a thread): which field is the body, who wrote it, which side is ours; what is left out is read from the fields.

body.description: The message's text: a text or markdown field (or a string).

author.description: Who wrote it: a field that refers to User, or an email field.

side.description: Which side a message is on: a two-valued choice field, and the value that is our side.

field.description: A choice field with two values.

ours.description: The value that means our side (shown on the right).

fields.description: Two or more of the model's stored fields, unique together.

scope.description: owner: among one owner's records; app: in the whole app. Left out, as the access says, like a field's unique: true.

unique.description: Fields unique together, e.g. [[customer, number]]: no two records hold the same values in all of them; { fields: [customer, number], scope: app } says where (owner: among one owner's records; app: in the whole app).

capacity.description: At most max records per record that per refers to, e.g. { per: session, max: session.capacity }: a booking's places.

per.description: A required reference of this model.

max.description: A whole number, or a whole-number field of the referenced record, "reference.field".

closes.description: Until when a record may be added: a date-time of the referenced record ("session.startsAt"), as it is or a period before it ("2 hours before session.startsAt").

cancelUntil.description: Until when a record's owner may delete it ("24 hours before session.startsAt"); roles that delete everyone's pass.

where.description: Only records with these choice or yes/no values count.

schedule.description: Its records are people (or rooms, chairs) whose time is booked, e.g. { hours: { mon-fri: "09:00-17:00" }, breaks: "12:00-12:30", gap: 10, away: TimeOff }.

hours.description: The weekly hours in the app's time zone: a weekday or a range of them (mon-fri) to a span ("09:00-17:00") or a list of spans. A day not named is closed.

breaks.description: Spans kept free every open day: "12:00-12:30", or a list of them.

gap.description: Minutes kept free after each booking.

resource.description: Its reference to this model; left out, its only one.

from.description: When the time away starts; left out, its first date-and-time field.

until.description: When it ends; left out, its second date-and-time field.

away.description: A model whose records block time (days off, holidays): its reference to this model and two date-time fields, from and until. Its name alone takes its one reference here and its first two date-time fields; { model, resource, from, until } says them.

occupies.description: Each record takes a scheduled record's time, e.g. { resource: barber, starts: startsAt, duration: service.minutes, while: { status: [requested, confirmed] }, cancelUntil: 12h }.

resource.description: A required reference of this model to a model with a schedule.

starts.description: A date-and-time field: when the time is taken.

duration.description: Minutes: a whole-number field of this model, or of a record it refers to ("service.minutes").

while.description: Only records with these choice or yes/no values take the time; the others free it.

cancelUntil.description: How long before the start the record's owner may cancel it: "30m", "12h" or "2d". Without it, until the start.

cancelTo.description: The value the owner's Cancel sets, outside while; needed when several values are outside it.

id.description: A short name to refer to the rule by.

actions.description: Operations of the application beyond create, edit and delete.

additionalProperties.description: Custom (custom: true, with input and output) or standard (on, when, set).

on.description: A standard action: the model whose record it changes.

when.description: Offered and allowed only for records with these choice values (or lists of them) or yes/no values, e.g. { status: [investigating, identified] }.

set.description: The new values: a literal the field accepts, a formula on the record as it was, or nothing to ask the person for it, e.g. { status: canceled, cancelReason: }.

add.description: Related records to create with the change, one per model that refers to this one, e.g. { IncidentUpdate: { status: resolved, at: NOW() } }.

copy.description: A new record from this one instead of a change: what differs, as in set (a value, a formula, ME() or nothing to ask); {} copies as is.

with.description: Lists of the model whose records a copy takes along, e.g. [lines].

output.description: The values the action returns, if any.

allow.description: Only these roles may run the action (admins always can).

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Domain rules in plain language. A rule does nothing by itself until something implements it: the models read them when drafting and changing the app, and the advice notes point at them.
examples: An order over 1000 needs a manager's approval before it ships.

id.description: A short name to refer to the rule by.

outgoing.description: Who is told when something happens to a record: a mail to the owner, a role or an address on the record; or a signed call to a named target.

when.description: What happens: "<Model> created", "<Model> changed" or "<Model> deleted", or the name of a standard action, e.g. "Booking created" or "resolve".

where.description: Only for records with these values, e.g. { status: confirmed }; a change counts when the record comes to fit them.

fields.description: For "<Model> changed": only a change of one of these fields counts, e.g. [startsAt].

to.description: "mail", or the name of a target whose address and secret are settings.

recipient.description: For mail: owner, a role, an email field or a field that refers to User, one reference away (customer.email), or a list field and then the owner or an address of each of its records (bookings.owner).

incoming.description: Addresses other services call (/incoming/<name>, each with its own secret): one record per call, or the call handed to code.

create.description: The model a call adds a record of.

set.description: The record's values: a literal, a formula (NOW()), or a text with {path} from the call's JSON ("{check.name} is down").

custom.description: Hand the verified call to src/custom/incoming/<name>.ts.

signed.description: A sha256 signature of the body, made with the secret.

header.description: The header the secret or signature comes in.

id.description: The call's own id, e.g. "{event.id}": a repeat is not acted on.

as.description: The role the call acts as (admin when not said).

mail.description: The call's body is a mail (from, to, subject, text, html, attachments).

fields.description: For a mail: the fields its parts go to.

from.description: An email field for the sender.

subject.description: A text field for the subject.

body.description: A text or markdown field for the mail's text.

attachments.description: A file or files field for its attachments.

reply.description: For a mail: what a mail of one of its records' threads becomes (a reply, by its headers or the subject's [app #id] tag), instead of a new record.

create.description: The model a reply becomes; it refers to the entry's own once.

fields.description: For a mail: the fields its parts go to.

from.description: An email field for the sender.

subject.description: A text field for the subject.

body.description: A text or markdown field for the mail's text.

attachments.description: A file or files field for its attachments.

set.description: The reply's other values, e.g. { direction: in }.

then.description: Values set on the record it joins, e.g. { status: open }.

queries.description: Records chosen or ordered by code in src/custom/queries/.

id.description: A short name to refer to the rule by.

pages.description: The application's pages. Each page uses one pattern: crud, landing, dashboard, settings, onboarding, users, data, review, calendar, calculator, articles, custom, legal or order.

route.description: Defaults to / plus the page name.

crud.description: A model to list, view, create, edit and delete.

landing.description: Sections of a landing page, in order: hero, features, records, pricing, testimonials, faq, callToAction, contact, gallery, footer, calculator, custom.

records.description: A model whose records the section shows.

search.description: A records section with a search box, leading to the model's list page.

filters.description: A records section's filters (fields of the model), leading to its list page.

where.description: A records section shows only records with these choice values (or lists of them) or yes/no values, e.g. { status: [investigating, identified] }.

button.description: The page the section's button opens.

shortcuts.description: A hero's shortcuts: up to four pages, shown as round icons.

limit.description: A records section: how many it shows.

form.description: A contact section's form: the model visitors add a record of.

fields.description: Fields as a model's: entered ones are the inputs, formula fields the results.

examples.description: Inputs and the results they must give; each becomes a test.

calculator.description: Inputs and results computed as you type, stored nowhere.

custom.description: A section of your own: the component in src/custom/sections/<Name>.tsx.

dashboard.description: Tiles of a dashboard, in order: numbers, charts by month, latest records.

count.description: Count a model's records, e.g. Invoice.

sum.description: Sum a number field, e.g. Invoice.total.

where.description: Only records with these choice values or yes/no values.

by.description: A date field: one bar per month.

limit.description: A list: how many records it shows.

settings.description: A model with one record per user (private data) or per app (shared): the page edits it.

onboarding.description: Fills the settings record in steps after the first sign-in.

model.description: The model of the settings record.

steps.description: The steps in order, each with the fields it asks for.

users.description: Who has access: invite people by email with a role, change roles and remove users. For admins, unless the page's access says otherwise.

data.description: An administrator's view of the app's data: all (every model) or a list of models, each with its records to find, open, change and delete. For admins, unless the page's access says otherwise.

review.description: The pictures and files waiting for review, to approve or reject with a reason: all (every model with review) or a list of models. For admins and the roles granted review in smithable.auth.yml.

oneOf.description: A model whose records have one date or date-time field.

model.description: The model whose records the calendar shows.

starts.description: The date or date-time field that places a record.

ends.description: An end field of the same kind.

duration.description: Minutes: a whole-number field, here or one reference away (classType.durationMinutes).

title.description: What a block says: a field, or a reference's title.

calendar.description: A model's records in a week or month calendar.

fields.description: Fields as a model's: entered ones are the inputs, formula fields the results.

examples.description: Inputs and the results they must give; each becomes a test.

calculator.description: Inputs and results computed as you type, stored nowhere.

oneOf.description: A model with a title and a markdown body; its other parts are read from the fields' types (docs/design/inference.md).

model.description: The model whose records are the articles.

body.description: A markdown field: the article itself.

picture.description: A picture field shown with the article; none for no picture.

date.description: A date or date-time field: when it appeared; none for no date.

address.description: A unique string field: the article's address (/blog/<address>); none for the number.

summary.description: A string or text field shown in the list; none for the body's first paragraph.

author.description: A field that refers to the user who wrote it, shown with the article; none for no author.

articles.description: A model's records as articles: a blog, news or a knowledge base.

custom.description: A page of your own: the component in src/custom/pages/<Name>.tsx, created once as a stub; the route, access and menu entry stay Smithable's.

legal.description: A privacy page written from the app itself: who runs it, what it stores and why, cookies, mail, logs, your rights. The operator's details are texts in smithable.content.yml (operator: name, address, email, country, hosting).

order.description: A page where visitors choose records of one model and send them as one order of another, with its lines, in one write; the prices are read on the server.

from.description: The model people choose from (dishes): its one money field is the price, its one yes/no field says what is available.

price.description: The money field of "from" that is the price, when it has several.

quantity.description: The whole-number field of the lines' model that holds how many, when it has several; none for no quantity.

available.description: The yes/no field of "from" that says a record can be ordered, when it has several; none for always.

into.description: The model an order is (one record per order, numbered with sequence: true), whose one list holds the lines.

ask.description: The order's fields the customer fills, in this order (name, phone, wanted, note).

hours.description: When orders are taken, in the app's time zone: a day or a range of days to a span or a list of spans, e.g. { mon-thu: "11:00-20:00", sat: ["10:00-14:00", "17:00-22:00"] }. Without hours, always.

lead.description: Minutes from now to the earliest time a customer may want the order.

actions.description: Actions offered on the page, as buttons.

search.description: Fields the list can be searched by, e.g. [name, email].

filters.description: Fields the list can be filtered by: choices and references as chips, numbers and dates as a range, yes/no as a toggle.

sortable.description: Fields the list can be sorted by, either way, from a Sort by control.

mine.description: The page lists only the viewer's own records (my items, my orders); it needs sign-in.

favorites.description: true: a heart on each record and a Saved view of the list; only: a list of the viewer's saved records.

to.description: owner, or a user field of the model.

keep.description: A model a copy of each message is stored in.

contact.description: A contact block on the record page that mails the record's owner (or the user a field names): owner, a field, or { to, keep }.
